etymologies.etymologyHTML: Recorded in English from 1433, "income from property or possessions", from Middle French revenue, from Old French [Term?] (“a return”) (modern French revenu), the prop. feminine past participle of revenir (“come back”) (=modern French), from Latin revenire (“to return, come back”), from re- (“back”) +‎ venire (“to come”).

definitions.definition: The income returned by an investment.

quote.citation: 2021 September 15, Laura Martin, “How talent shows became TV's most bizarre programmes”, in BBC‎[1]:
quote.text: In the seventh series of The X Factor in the UK, it's estimated the phone votes brought in more than £5.4 million in revenue.

definitions.definition: The total income received from a given source.
All income generated for some political entity's treasury by taxation and other means.
(accounting) The net income from normal business operations; net sales.

quote.text: What, no revenue of praise for him who is our gracious Lord and King! He doth not exact from us any servile labor, but simply saith, “Who so offereth praise glorifieth me.”
